subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Water Treatment: Pump-Driven Purification
description: A 60-second lesson on Water Treatment: Pump-Driven Purification.

hook.text: Clean tap water doesn't happen by accident. Pumps push it through every step.

buildup.text: Raw water is pumped through screens, settling tanks, and sand filters.

discovery.text: Final disinfection and high-pressure pumping deliver clean water to your tap.

twist.text: A city water system can lose 20% of its water to leaking old pipes.

climax.text: Pressure management and leak detection are saving billions of liters a year.

punchline.text: Every glass of clean water rode a pump to reach you.

quiz.question: Why is pressure management important in city water systems?
options: Higher pressure improves water taste and quality
Managing pressure reduces leaks in aging pipes, saving water and energy
Pumps last longer when they run at maximum pressure
